items.passage: "Your heel is worn on the left, as it always was," said Anacleto, without lifting his eyes from the awl. Pavel had set the boot on the counter of the little stall in Oaxaca and waited, as if nine years were a matter that required no remark. In their youth the two men had baked on opposite corners of the same street, each rising earlier to spite the other, each claiming the better crust. Now Anacleto mended shoes, and Pavel, it seemed, had come back with nothing but a cracked boot. Neither spoke of the ovens or of the winter Pavel vanished. Yet when the work was done, Anacleto refused the coins, and Pavel, after a long moment, left on the counter a small loaf wrapped in paper, still warm. Outside, a cart of marigolds rattled past toward the market, its driver singing off-key.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To show two former rivals renewing a bond through gestures, not explanations
To recount how a baker who vanished for years came back to have a boot repaired
To explain why Anacleto abandoned baking and took up the trade of mending shoes
To suggest that old quarrels always fade once enough years have quietly passed
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 두 사람은 서로를 이기려 일찍 일어나던 경쟁 제빵사였다고 소개되고, 뒷부분에서 Anacleto는 돈을 받지 않고 Pavel은 따뜻한 빵을 남긴다. 두 사람은 과거를 말하지 않지만 이 대비를 통해 말없는 화해가 드러나므로 A가 정답이다. B는 일화만 요약했을 뿐 서술 목적을 담지 못한다. C는 지문 소재를 쓰지만 직업을 바꾼 이유는 지문의 관심사가 아니며, D는 지문을 넘어선 일반적 교훈이다.

items.passage: When Hassan and I first climbed the wall of the abandoned orchard behind his father's rental houses in Colombo, we were twelve and wanted only mangoes. Within a summer we had cleared the weeds, propped the sagging trees, and sold enough fruit at the junction to pay my family's rent for a month. I remember that I was proud, and that Hassan was prouder. But success has a way of being noticed. His father began asking what the orchard earned, and my mother began worrying aloud that we owed him for every mango. Hassan and I still met under the trees, though now we counted the fruit before we talked. Haoran, my younger brother, stopped coming with us altogether. Years later, I still keep a bent pruning hook on a nail by my door, its handle wrapped in blue electrical tape.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To describe how two children cleared an overgrown orchard and sold its mangoes
To reflect on how a shared success drew a friendship into two families' tensions
To argue that the orchard's owner, not his tenants' children, should have restored it
To suggest that every childhood friendship eventually yields to adult concerns
items.explanation: 앞부분은 두 아이가 과수원을 함께 살려 낸 자랑스러운 성공을 보여 주고, 뒷부분은 집주인 아버지와 세입자 어머니가 수익과 빚을 따지기 시작하자 아이들도 이야기 전에 과일부터 세게 되었다고 대비한다. 따라서 공동의 성공이 두 집안의 긴장 속으로 우정을 끌어들였다는 B가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, C는 소재를 쓰지만 지문에 없는 주장을 목적으로 삼는다. D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Auckland summers, in my memory, smelled of hot tar and of the rooftop water tank where I hid after my father left. Kainoa, who sold fish from the back of a van on our street, found me there one afternoon holding my father's old diving watch, its strap cracked. He did not ask about it. Instead he handed me a snapper to carry home and said the watch still kept good time. For weeks afterward he timed his deliveries by it, calling up to the roof for the hour, as though the watch had a job worth doing. I began to wind it each morning without being told. Kamal, my cousin, thought the whole arrangement ridiculous. Below the tank, the neighbor's lemon tree dropped its fruit into the gutter, and nobody gathered it.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To recount how a fish seller found a boy hiding on a roof with a cracked watch
To explain why the narrator's cousin disapproved of the fish seller's arrangement
To show how a neighbor's quiet attention gave an absent father's watch a new use
To suggest that grief always eases once a child is given ordinary work to do
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 아버지가 떠난 뒤 아버지의 시계를 들고 숨어 있었고, Kainoa는 아무것도 묻지 않는다. 뒷부분에서 Kainoa가 그 시계로 배달 시간을 물으며 시계에 할 일을 주자 화자는 스스로 시계를 감기 시작한다. 두 근거를 이으면 이웃의 조용한 관심이 시계에 새 쓰임을 주었다는 C가 정답이다. A는 일화 요약, B는 소재를 쓰지만 목적이 다르고, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: On her first morning in Rotterdam, Hana stood in the customs line with her boots tied to her duffel bag, the same boots she had barely worn all last season on the bench. Lars, her new coach, waited beyond the glass with a club scarf folded over his arm. When the officer asked the purpose of her visit, Hana said work, then corrected herself and said football. Months earlier she had told a reporter that she no longer knew what she was for. At the gate, Lars offered to carry the duffel, but Hana shook her head and slung it over her own shoulder, boots knocking against her back. Outside, a tram slid past the terminal, its windows fogged with breath.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Hana most likely correct her answer to the officer?
options: She is nervous that the officer will doubt her stated reason for entering the country.
She hopes Lars will overhear her and decide to place her in the starting lineup.
She has been told by the club that work visas are not issued to visiting athletes.
She wants to claim football as her identity again after a purposeless season.
items.explanation: 첫 문장에서 Hana의 부츠는 지난 시즌 벤치에 앉아 거의 신지 못한 것이었고, 넷째 문장에서 그녀는 자신이 무엇을 위한 존재인지 모르겠다고 말한 적이 있다. 두 단서를 이으면 '일' 대신 '축구'라고 고친 것은 축구를 다시 자기 정체성으로 붙잡으려는 동기임을 알 수 있어 D가 정답이다. A는 다른 감정을 동기로 삼았고, B는 행동의 결과를 동기로 착각했다. C는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.

items.passage: Who leaves a recipe tin buried under a ferry terminal? Kalani asked herself this as she knelt in the sand the storm had stripped from around the pilings on Maui. The tin was rusted, but inside, wrapped in oilcloth, were cards in her grandmother's slanted hand. Aunt Mattie, who ran the terminal snack counter and allowed no one else near her stove, had always said there were no family recipes, only work. Kalani turned one card over and found Mattie's own childhood initials penciled in a corner beside a smear of what might have been coconut. She tucked the tin into her apron instead of carrying it straight to her aunt, and that afternoon she cooked the first recipe alone, before Mattie's shift began. Gulls circled the docked ferry, waiting for the passengers' scraps.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Kalani most likely cook the recipe before her aunt arrives?
options: She expects her aunt to deny the recipes and wants to cook them before that happens.
She feels guilty for digging under the terminal and fears her aunt will scold her for it.
She wants to earn a permanent place beside her aunt at the snack counter's stove.
She has been instructed by a note in the tin to cook her grandmother's recipes in secret.
items.explanation: Mattie는 자기 화덕에 아무도 들이지 않고 집안 요리법 같은 건 없다고 늘 말해 왔다. 그런데 Kalani는 카드에서 Mattie의 어릴 적 이니셜을 발견하므로, 이모가 요리법의 존재를 알면서도 부정해 왔음을 짐작한다. 두 단서를 이으면 이모가 부정하기 전에 직접 요리해 보려 했다는 A가 정답이다. B는 다른 감정, C는 행동의 결과를 동기로 착각한 것이며, D는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.

items.passage: After the rains ended, Zawadi went to the seed cooperative in Nairobi to collect his late grandfather's share, and Neema, who had sorted beans beside the old man for forty years, met him at the door with a ledger. They argued first about the jar labels, which Zawadi wanted printed and Neema insisted on writing by hand. Her voice was sharp, but she kept touching the shelf where his grandfather's chair had stood. Zawadi noticed that she had saved the speckled cowpeas his grandfather favored in a separate tin, tied with the same frayed string he had always used. When he finally conceded the labels, Neema laughed softly and pressed the tin into his hands without a word. He stood holding it, feeling its weight shift as the seeds settled. In the yard, a boy was chasing a goat between the drying racks.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Irritable, dwelling on a stubborn quarrel over how the jar labels should be written
Tender, with brief surface bickering giving way to shared grief and affection
Combative, though softened at moments by small hints of fondness between the two
Celebratory, reflecting the cooperative's pride in a plentiful harvest after the rains
items.explanation: 라벨을 두고 다투는 장면과 날카로운 목소리에는 짜증이 드러나지만, Neema가 할아버지 의자가 있던 선반을 계속 만지고 그가 좋아하던 콩을 따로 챙겨 둔 장면에서는 슬픔과 애정이 더 두드러진다. 따라서 표면의 다툼이 공유된 슬픔과 애정으로 이어지는 다정한 어조라는 B가 정답이다. A는 덜 두드러진 정서만 말했고, C는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었다. D는 비가 그쳤다는 소재와 어울리지만 지문에 단서가 약하다.

items.passage: Three rules governed the waiting room on the fourth floor of the Istanbul hospital: no phones at the desk, one visitor per patient, and no food after eight. Nargis broke the third one by setting a paper bag of simit on the chair between herself and Burak, the brother she had not spoken to since their father's funeral. He glanced at it and did not take one. An hour later, when the nurse called their mother's name and mispronounced it, only Nargis noticed; Burak was already standing, but she corrected the nurse quietly so that he would not have to. On his way past, Burak nudged the bag back toward her side of the chair, one simit gone. Above the vending machine, a television played a cooking show with the sound turned off.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Nargis and Burak?
options: A sister keeps reaching out to a brother who remains entirely unmoved by her efforts.
A brother looks after a sister who depends on him to speak for her at the desk.
Estranged siblings are cautiously exchanging small kindnesses despite their silence.
Close siblings have always shared the duty of caring for their mother equally.
items.explanation: 두 사람은 아버지의 장례 이후 말을 하지 않은 사이지만, Nargis는 빵 봉지를 둘 사이에 놓고 간호사의 실수를 Burak 대신 조용히 바로잡는다. 뒤이어 Burak은 빵 하나를 먹고 봉지를 그녀 쪽으로 밀어 두어 작은 응답을 한다. 두 행동을 이어 읽으면 소원한 남매가 조심스럽게 작은 친절을 주고받는 관계라는 C가 정답이다. A는 한쪽 감정만 반영했고, B는 방향이 반대이며, D는 지문과 맞지 않는 일반적 통념이다.

items.passage: Parvin took the window seat on the night bus through Tehran, as she had since they were girls, and Aigerim, her twin, let her. Between them on the bench lay the folded plan of their mother's house, each room already marked in two colors of ink. Aigerim had told no one that she had failed the licensing exam that afternoon, the one she had promised to pass before they sold anything. When Parvin asked whether she wanted the room with the garden door, Aigerim said it did not matter, and Parvin, without looking up, drew a line that gave her both that room and the study beside it. "You always liked the garden," Parvin said, as if the matter had been settled long ago. Outside, shuttered shops slid by under orange streetlights.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Parvin and Aigerim?
options: A sister resents always yielding the window seat to her more demanding twin.
Aigerim shields Parvin from bad news by quietly handling the house herself.
Rivals compete over which of them will inherit the larger share of the house.
Twins know each other so well that one quietly gives way without being asked.
items.explanation: 첫 문장에서 Aigerim은 어릴 때부터 그랬듯 창가 자리를 Parvin에게 내주고, 뒤에서는 Aigerim이 상관없다고 하자 Parvin이 묻지도 않고 정원 방과 서재를 모두 그녀에게 준다. 이를 이어 읽으면 서로를 깊이 알아 말없이 양보하는 쌍둥이 관계임을 알 수 있어 D가 정답이다. A는 한쪽 감정만 반영했고, B는 보살핌의 방향을 뒤집었다. C는 유산 분할이라는 소재에서 나온 일반적 통념이다.

items.passage: When Siti walked along the seaside promenade in Hanoi each evening after working in Dewi's new garden, she carried the same black umbrella, furled tight, though the sky over the water was clear. Dewi, who had bought the house only that spring, asked once why she never opened it. Siti said it was for a storm that had not arrived. Their friend in the hospital on the hill had asked them both, that week, whether the doctors were hiding anything. Dewi wanted to tell her plainly. Siti only tightened the strap on the umbrella and said there was still time. On Thursday, rain came in sideways off the sea, and Siti stood under the awning of a noodle stall with the umbrella still closed, rain soaking her sleeves, until Dewi took it from her and opened it over them both. Below the railing, fishing boats knocked together in the swell.
items.question: In the text, the closed umbrella most likely represents
options: Siti's reluctance to face and share a painful truth even once it can't be avoided.
Siti's practical habit of preparing carefully for sudden changes in coastal weather.
the new house Dewi bought and the garden Siti tends there each working day.
Siti's wish to protect Dewi from the storms that often strike the promenade.
items.explanation: Siti는 맑은 날에도 우산을 접은 채 들고 다니며 아직 오지 않은 폭풍을 위한 것이라고 말한다. 친구에게 진실을 말하자는 Dewi의 말에 Siti는 우산 끈을 조이며 아직 시간이 있다고 하고, 막상 비가 오자 우산을 펴지 못한다. 이 두 장면을 이으면 우산은 피할 수 없게 된 뒤에도 고통스러운 진실을 마주하고 전하기를 주저하는 Siti의 마음을 상징하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 문자 그대로의 해석이고, C와 D는 지문의 반복 이미지와 연결되지 않는다.

items.passage: Years later, Emre would still remember the cairn. When he came back from the army to the edge of the salt flat outside Cairo, he expected Hala to meet him with the cold silence she had promised in her last letter, the one that called him a deserter of the family. Instead she walked him past the drying pans to the low pile of stones he had begun as a boy, now taller than her waist. "One for every week you were gone," she said, setting another on top. He counted without meaning to; there were no gaps. That evening she showed him the ledgers she had kept for their father's salt works, every column balanced, a line left blank beside each month for his signature. Wind moved across the flat, lifting a thin white dust that settled on their shoes.
items.question: In the text, the cairn most likely represents
options: the resentment Hala had built up toward Emre during the weeks he was gone
Hala's steady, unbroken faithfulness to her brother throughout his absence
the family salt works that Emre hoped one day to take over from their father
Emre's boyhood ambition to build something lasting out on the salt flat
items.explanation: Hala는 오빠가 떠나 있던 매주 돌을 하나씩 올렸고, Emre가 세어 보니 빠진 주가 없었다. 또 그녀는 매달 오빠의 서명 칸을 비워 둔 장부를 보여 주어, 차갑게 맞으리라던 예상과 달리 그를 기다려 왔음을 드러낸다. 두 단서를 이으면 돌무더기는 오빠에 대한 꾸준하고 끊김 없는 충실함을 상징하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 편지의 표현에만 기댄 오독이고, C와 D는 지문 소재를 쓰지만 돌무더기의 의미와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Tell your mother you were with me the whole time, Weiqi said, pinning a wet shirt to the rooftop line above the Taipei alley. Zihan, who had wandered off the trail above the city for six hours before the ranger found her, watched the shirts snap in the wind. She knew the story was false; Weiqi had found her alone, mud to the knees, far from any marked path. But Weiqi said the truth would only get Zihan's hiking permit revoked and his own patrol questioned. Zihan agreed, and the lie settled between them like a stone in a shoe, small and impossible to forget with every step. All that evening she caught herself rehearsing it, changing a detail, then changing it back. Across the alley, a neighbor's radio played an old ballad over the rattle of an air conditioner.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “like a stone in a shoe” most nearly suggests that the lie is
options: a minor but constant discomfort that Zihan cannot stop noticing
a heavy burden that keeps Zihan from walking the trails again
a secret that Zihan has nearly forgotten by the end of the evening
a protective weight that steadies Zihan against her mother's anger
items.explanation: 이 비유 바로 뒤에는 작지만 걸음마다 잊을 수 없다는 설명이 붙어 있다. 또 그날 저녁 Zihan이 거짓말을 계속 되뇌며 세부를 바꿨다가 되돌리는 모습이 나와, 거짓말이 작지만 끊임없이 신경 쓰이는 불편함임을 뒷받침한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 비유를 문자 그대로 무거운 짐으로 읽었고, C는 계속 되뇐다는 내용과 반대이며, D는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Did anyone else see the case fall? Layla asked the depot clerk in Beirut, though she already knew the answer. Her violin had slipped from the overhead rack when the bus braked, and Sigrid, her teacher, insisted that Layla had left the case unlatched. Layla remembered fastening both clasps. The driver said a passenger had bumped it; a woman by the window said no one had touched it at all. Each account was confident, and each was different, so that the truth seemed to splinter into pieces too small to hold. Sigrid examined the cracked bridge with her usual severity, then said only that bridges could be replaced and that Layla would practice on the spare instrument until Friday. Outside, buses idled in their bays, exhaust drifting over the ticket windows.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “splinter into pieces too small to hold” most nearly suggests that
options: the violin was so badly damaged that it could never be repaired
the conflicting accounts broke the event into fragments no one could join
Layla was too upset to recall what she had done with the case's clasps
the witnesses were careless people whose statements deserved no attention
items.explanation: 앞 문장들에서 Sigrid, Layla, 운전기사, 창가의 여자가 저마다 다른 이야기를 하고, 이 비유는 모두 확신에 차 있지만 서로 다르다는 문장에 이어 나온다. 그러므로 진실이 쪼개진다는 표현은 엇갈린 증언 때문에 사건을 하나의 이야기로 맞출 수 없다는 뜻이며 B가 정답이다. A는 깨진 브리지에 끌려 비유를 문자 그대로 읽었고, Sigrid가 브리지는 교체할 수 있다고 한 것과도 맞지 않는다. C와 D는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
Pass me the list, Marta said, and I did,
my mother's pencil hovering over names
while snow sealed the cabin door outside Samarkand.
Aydin's family, she wrote, then paused,
the letter I never sent her folded in my coat
like a coal I kept from going out
and kept from touching.
We counted chairs. We argued over lamb.
She did not ask, and I did not offer,
though twice her hand found my sleeve.
By the stove the kettle ticked as it cooled,
and the window held a square of blue dusk.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “like a coal I kept from going out” most nearly suggests that the speaker
options: wishes she could finally forget a painful memory from the past
intends to raise an old grudge with her mother at the wedding
keeps an apology alive while not yet being ready to deliver it
plans to present the letter to her mother after the ceremony
items.explanation: 부치지 못한 편지는 꺼지지 않게 지켜 온 석탄에 비유되는데, 바로 다음 행에서 화자는 그것을 만지지도 않았다고 말한다. 뒤에서도 어머니는 묻지 않고 화자도 꺼내지 않아, 사과의 마음은 간직하지만 아직 전하지 못하는 상태임이 드러난다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 잊고 싶다는 반대 방향이고, B는 원한이라는 근거 없는 해석이며, D는 지문에 없는 계획이다.

items.passage: Chess rivals make poor confidants. I learned this at four in the morning in my aunt's bakery in Albuquerque, where Dainius and I had met to argue, as usual, though not about openings. My younger brother had asked each of us, separately, whether he should quit the club after losing every game of the season. Dainius wanted to tell him the truth: that he played too fast. I wanted to tell him he would improve. Between the cooling racks we circled the question like two kings in an endgame, each step careful, neither willing to come close enough to be checked. By the time the first tray of conchas came out, we had agreed on nothing except that my brother deserved one answer, not two. Kaya, my aunt, unlocked the front door and flipped the sign.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “circled the question like two kings in an endgame” most nearly suggests that the narrator and Dainius
options: played a slow game of chess while waiting for the bakery to open
competed fiercely to prove who understood the brother better
paced the bakery restlessly because they were tired and anxious
approached the problem warily, each avoiding an exposed position
items.explanation: 비유 바로 뒤에서 두 사람은 한 걸음씩 조심하며 체크당할 만큼 가까이 다가가지 않으려 한다. 또 결국 아무것도 합의하지 못했다는 내용이 이어져, 서로 공격받을 입장을 피하며 문제를 조심스럽게 다루었음을 알 수 있다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 비유를 실제 체스 경기로 읽었고, B는 격렬한 경쟁이라는 점에서 조심스러운 태도와 맞지 않으며, C는 피곤과 불안이라는 근거 없는 이유를 끌어왔다.

items.passage: A folded bus ticket was all Solange ever left me. I had been her teacher for two years in the hills above Marseille, and in that time she had not said a word in class, though her essays ran long and fierce in pencil. On her last day before her family moved north, we waited together at the mountain bus stop, I with my briefcase, she with a backpack so full it seemed to lean on her. I had prepared a small speech about the proper way to say goodbye. I never gave it. When the bus came, she pressed the ticket into my hand, and on its back she had written a single line of thanks, the letters pressed so hard they had nearly torn through, a whole conversation squeezed into the width of a thumb. Genevieve, my colleague, later framed it for me. That spring, the broom on the hillside bloomed early and yellow.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a whole conversation squeezed into the width of a thumb” most nearly suggests that
options: the brief note carried all that Solange had never said aloud
Solange's handwriting was too small for the teacher to read
Solange regretted not having had more time to talk at the stop
the teacher squeezed in a hurried final lesson before the bus
items.explanation: 앞에서 Solange는 2년 동안 수업 시간에 한마디도 하지 않았지만 글은 길고 강렬했다고 소개된다. 마지막에 그녀가 종이를 뚫을 듯 눌러 쓴 감사 한 줄은 그동안 말로 하지 않은 모든 것을 담은 것이므로, 엄지 너비에 압축된 대화라는 비유는 A를 뜻한다. B는 비유를 글씨 크기로 문자 그대로 읽었고, C는 지문에 없는 후회를 끌어왔다. D는 '압축'이라는 표현만 빌린 오답이다.

items.passage: Lan had come back to help with the harvest. Friedrich, her old teacher, owned the last small vineyard on the slope above the Elbe outside Hamburg, and every September he still checked each row himself. This year, however, she found that he had already sold the lower terraces to a developer, without a word to her or to the cooperative that had tended them for a decade. When she confronted him among the crates, he did not apologize or explain; he simply named the price and the date, as if reporting the weather. His manner was so ______ that Lan wondered whether he had expected any objection at all. They worked the rest of the afternoon without speaking, filling crate after crate with dark fruit.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: self-reproachful
matter-of-fact
defensive
hesitant
items.explanation: Friedrich는 사과도 설명도 하지 않고 날씨를 전하듯 가격과 날짜만 말한다. 그래서 Lan은 그가 반대를 예상하기는 했는지 의아해하므로, 빈칸에는 감정 없이 사실만 전하는 태도를 뜻하는 B가 알맞다. A는 스스로를 탓하는 태도로, 사과하지 않았다는 내용과 맞지 않는다. C는 그럴듯하지만 그는 변명하거나 해명하지 않았고, D는 머뭇거림 없이 말했다는 점과 어긋난다.

items.passage: Chengdu was wet that week, and the back room of Shuang's tailoring shop smelled of steam and wool. Baoyu came in without knocking, as he had for forty years, and sat on the stool by the cutting table. He had come, at last, to apologize for the wedding he had missed, though the couple in question now had grandchildren. Shuang listened, pinning a sleeve, and when Baoyu finished she neither forgave nor rebuked him. She only said that the suit he had been measured for that spring still hung in the cupboard, unclaimed. The apology, offered so late, seemed less a repair than a ______ gesture, one that honored a debt neither of them could still collect. Outside, a bicycle bell rang twice in the lane.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: generous
opportunistic
ceremonial
reckless
items.explanation: 사과는 결혼식이 있은 지 수십 년이 지나 너무 늦게 왔고, Shuang은 용서도 꾸짖음도 하지 않는다. 빈칸 뒤에서는 이제 누구도 받아 낼 수 없는 빚을 기리는 행위라고 설명하므로, 실질적인 회복보다 형식적·상징적 의미의 몸짓이라는 C가 알맞다. A는 그럴듯하지만 관대함은 지문의 초점이 아니다. B는 이득을 노린 몸짓이라는 뜻이지만 지문에서 얻을 것이 없다고 하므로 맞지 않고, D는 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
"Hand me the small screwdriver," Salma says,
and Karim does, though he keeps one eye on the door
and on the scholarship letter waiting in his bag,
unopened, offering a school in another city.
She is new here, and teaches only on Saturdays,
bending over Marrakesh radios with their backs pried off.
He has not trusted a teacher in years.
Yet when the dead set crackles into a voice,
his guard drops for a moment, ______,
and he laughs before he can stop himself.
Then he straightens, wipes his hands, and says nothing.
In the alley, a cart of oranges rolls past the open door.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: intentionally
reluctantly
irreversibly
involuntarily
items.explanation: Karim은 몇 년 동안 선생님을 믿지 않았지만, 고장 난 라디오에서 소리가 나자 스스로 멈추기도 전에 웃어 버린다. 이어 곧바로 몸을 바로 세우고 아무 말도 하지 않으므로, 경계가 의도와 상관없이 순간적으로 풀렸다는 D가 알맞다. A는 의도적이라는 뜻이라 '멈추기도 전에'와 어긋나고, C는 '잠시'라는 표현과 모순된다. B는 그럴듯하지만 마지못해 하는 의식적 선택을 뜻해 저절로 일어난 반응과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: When my grandfather died, his surveyor's measuring wheel went not to my father, who had walked fields beside him for thirty years, but to Jianguo, the boy who delivered our groceries. My grandmother, Xiulan, said only that the will was the will. I resented it for a long time. Then one evening at the soccer field near our building in Shanghai, I watched Jianguo roll the wheel along the touchline at dusk, marking out a pitch for the neighborhood children with the same slow care my grandfather had used. He checked each length twice and chalked each corner by hand. Watching him, I began to see the gift as less a mistake than a ______ choice: my grandfather had given the wheel to the one person who would still use it. Floodlights flickered on above the stands, and moths gathered around them.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: deliberate
careless
sentimental
hasty
items.explanation: 화자는 처음에 측량 바퀴가 잘못 상속되었다고 원망했지만, Jianguo가 할아버지처럼 정성껏 바퀴를 쓰는 모습을 보고 생각을 바꾼다. 빈칸 뒤에서 할아버지가 그것을 계속 쓸 단 한 사람에게 주었다고 설명하므로, 실수가 아니라 의도된 선택이라는 A가 알맞다. B와 D는 '실수'와 같은 쪽의 의미라 대비 구조에 맞지 않는다. C는 그럴듯하지만 감상이 아니라 실제 쓰임을 고려한 선택이라는 내용과 어긋난다.

items.passage: Years later, I still think about the tea. Folasade kept my uncle's bookbinding workshop in Lagos, and I was apprenticed there the summer a surveyor named Kwame came to measure the building for the new road. Each afternoon Folasade brought him tea in her best cup and let him rest in the cool back room among the stacked signatures. My uncle was certain she was flattering Kwame so that he would draw the boundary line a little farther from our door. I watched closely, but she never once mentioned the line, and when his map was finished she did not ask to see it. Her kindness, I decided, was ______; it asked for nothing in return. On the workbench, a half-sewn ledger waited under its press.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: calculated
sincere
excessive
reluctant
items.explanation: 삼촌은 Folasade가 경계선을 유리하게 그리게 하려고 측량사에게 아첨한다고 의심했다. 하지만 화자가 지켜본 결과 그녀는 경계선을 한 번도 언급하지 않았고 완성된 지도도 보려 하지 않았으며, 빈칸 뒤에서도 아무 대가를 바라지 않았다고 말하므로 B가 알맞다. A는 삼촌의 의심에서 나온 그럴듯한 오답이지만 화자의 결론과 반대이다. C와 D는 지문에 근거가 없다.
